A1.justification: Both PDFs describe D2Dewarp and DocDewarpHV. All 10 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v3 were inspected, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Tables II-IV report original dewarping and OCR evaluations on DocUNet, DIR300, and DocReal; Tables V-VI report component ablations.

after.justification: Tables 2-6 retain original benchmark and ablation results. Tables 2-3 additionally report DocScanner retraining experiments, and Section 4.4 reports processing speed.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, dual line decoders, pooling and attention fusion, deformation-field prediction, and training-loss equations remain unchanged. Added pooling/output descriptions clarify the existing method. Convolutional downsampling is discussed as a possible enhancement, without establishing its adoption.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 114,385-image DocDewarpHV dataset, the same source document datasets, and the DocUNet, DIR300, and DocReal benchmarks. The revised qualitative examples remain within previously represented text-rich, figure-heavy, and background-interference conditions.

E2.justification: The quantitative comparator sets are substantially reduced. Table II to Table 2 removes DocUNet, FCN-based, Piece-Wise, DocTr, DDCP, FDRNet, and DocTr-Plus, while adding DvD. DIR300 loses DocProj, DewarpNet, DocTr, DDCP, and DocRes; DocReal loses DocTr, DDCP, FTDR, and DocRes. Some removed quantitative comparators remain in qualitative figures.

E3.justification: v3 adds a controlled comparison by retraining DocScanner on DocDewarpHV and evaluating it on DocUNet and DIR300. It also introduces parameter-count and per-image runtime comparisons. The proposed model's training settings, benchmark sizes, OCR subsets, and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations retain their results. v3 adds a training-data control, a focused horizontal-rectification comparison in Figure 5, and a text-dense/text-sparse illustration in Figure 6. It removes the unclear-boundary failure example from v1 Figure 8 while retaining the background-text failure case.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-training run counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. The newly reported average processing time does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The reported result set changes substantially through comparator-row removals, new DvD and retrained DocScanner scores, parameter counts, and runtime results. DocReal's distorted-input AD/ED/CER change from 0.771/1500.56/0.5234 to 0.969/333.52/0.4432. DocTLNet's DIR300 CER changes from 0.1767 to 0.178, beyond equivalent rounding. D2Dewarp's benchmark and component-ablation scores remain unchanged apart from rounding.

T1.justification: v3 introduces an inconsistent formal indexing specification beside Equation 4: it states i belongs to {0,1,2,3}, while retaining the summation from i=1 to L and specifying L=4. Other mathematical expressions are equivalent; removal of the expanded standard BCE formulas does not constitute a substantive theoretical change.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same three contributions: dual-direction geometric representation, the HV Fusion Module, and a dataset with horizontal/vertical annotations. Claims of improved document flatness, readability, and state-of-the-art performance remain. The abstract's explicit mention of three benchmarks reflects coverage already present in v1.

C2.justification: v3 explains text-sparse difficulties through weaker line guidance, replacing v1's emphasis on difficult figure/table boundary detection. It expands the Chinese-document discussion with a proposed convolutional alternative and its computational cost, adds a speed-quality interpretation, and suggests foreground/UV information for background interference. The explicit irregular-boundary failure qualification is removed.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies pooled feature dimensions and deformation-field channels, and newly documents equal-count self-attention controls for existing ablations. Its abstract changes promised release to stated availability at the D2Dewarp repository, although future-release wording remains elsewhere; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Existing training hyperparameters and software versions are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including DocMamba, DocMatcher, DvD, and document enhancement/evaluation work, while removing DocProj, FDRNet, and several peripheral recognition references. It drops the explicit acknowledgment of RDGR's rule-based vertical information. The central positioning around complementary horizontal/vertical features remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, result discussions, limitations, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting and condensation. Related work gains thematic subdivisions, and ablations become part of the experimental-results subsection. The title, author order, and affiliation presentation also change, while much of the core method description is retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from an IEEE journal layout to a conference-style layout. Figure 3 gains feature labels and colored pathways, coordinated with colored equations. Qualitative panels are reduced or replaced, including removal of the separate DIR300 and DocReal comparison grids and addition of a local-crop comparison. Tables add a parameter column and consolidate metric columns.

improvement.justification: The same-training-data DocScanner comparison in Tables 2-3 addresses a confound left open in v1, while clearer fusion diagrams, disclosed ablation controls, and resource reporting improve interpretability. These gains are limited by reduced comparison and failure-case coverage, unspecified timing conditions, and the new Equation 4 indexing inconsistency. The central method and its performance evidence remain stable, supporting a modest overall improvement.
